title: Cocompletion of a homotopy-cocomplete cofibration category
statement:
Use quasicategories, mapping spaces, coherent functors and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with an initial object $0$ and classes $C,W$ of arrows. Assume: $C$ and $W$ contain isomorphisms and are closed under composition; $W$ is retract closed and has two-out-of-three; every object is cofibrant, meaning $0\to X\in C$; every arrow factors as a member of $C$ followed by a member of $W$; pushouts of members of $C$ exist and belong to $C$, and pushouts of members of $C\cap W$ belong to $C\cap W$. Suppose all $\mathcal U$-small coproducts exist, and the coproduct of any $\mathcal U$-small family of members of $C$ (respectively $C\cap W$) belongs to $C$ (respectively $C\cap W$). These are the all-cofibrant ordinary homotopy-cocomplete cofibration-category hypotheses.

Let $q:N(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A[W^{-1}]_\infty$ be a homotopy coherent localization, defined by its universal property on entire coherent functor categories, in a sufficiently large universe. Then $\mathcal A[W^{-1}]_\infty$ admits all $\mathcal U$-small coherent colimits. The functor $q$ carries $0$, $\mathcal U$-small coproduct cocones and pushout squares along members of $C$ to initial objects, coproduct cocones and pushout squares, respectively. If $\mathcal E$ is any infinity category admitting all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and $T:N(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal E$ inverts $W$ and preserves these initial objects, coproduct cocones and cofibration pushout squares, then its factorization $\overline T:\mathcal A[W^{-1}]_\infty\to\mathcal E$ preserves all $\mathcal U$-small coherent colimits. This assertion includes transformations: restriction identifies the full coherent functor category of colimit-preserving functors on the localization with the full subcategory of such homotopy-cocontinuous functors $T$.

source.place: Dual of Definition 7.7.2, Proposition 7.7.4 and Theorem 7.7.9, printed pp. 397-399; the all-cofibrant ordinary case of the cofibration-category axioms dual to section 7.4. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical cocompletion theorem.

proof.text: Put $L=\mathcal A[W^{-1}]_\infty$. Apply [lem-coef-brown-fibrant-localization-pullbacks] to $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$, with terminal object $0$ and fibrations $C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its terminal-map, pullback, trivial-pullback and weak-equivalence/fibration factorization hypotheses are respectively the initial-map, pushout, trivial-pushout and cofibration/weak-equivalence hypotheses of the item, with all arrows reversed. Isomorphisms and composition are in the specified classes, and $W^{\mathrm{op}}$ has two-out-of-three. Opposite localization is localization of the opposite: the universal property follows by taking opposites of coherent functor categories, $\operatorname{Fun}(B^{\mathrm{op}},E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(B,E^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Hence that node gives finite colimits in $L$, sends $0$ to an initial object, and sends every cofibration pushout square to a coherent pushout, including its cocone and naturality. These are coherent universal properties in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], not colimits of the ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: Dual finite-localization statement of Theorem 7.5.18, used in the proof of Proposition 7.7.4 Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Coproducts preserve $W$ under the item hypotheses, by the following explicit Brown argument. For $f:X\to Y$ in $W$, factor $(f,1_Y):X\amalg Y\to Y$ as $X\amalg Y\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $j\in C$ and $p\in W$. Each coproduct inclusion belongs to $C$, since it is a pushout of the other object's initial map. Thus $i=j\operatorname{in}_X$ and $s=j\operatorname{in}_Y$ belong to $C$; $pi=f$ and $ps=1_Y$ show by two-out-of-three that both belong to $W$. For a $\mathcal U$-small family $f_a$, perform this construction for each $a$. Then $\coprod_ai_a$ and $\coprod_as_a$ belong to $C\cap W$ by the assumed coproduct axiom, and $(\coprod_ap_a)(\coprod_as_a)=1$ forces $\coprod_ap_a\in W$. Therefore $\coprod_af_a=(\coprod_ap_a)(\coprod_ai_a)\in W$. All identities and compositions here are determined by coproduct coprojections using [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; no fibration, lifting property or functorial factorization is used. The empty family gives the identity of $0$.

source.place: Dual elementary Brown argument of Corollary 7.4.14, as used in Proposition 7.7.4 Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Fix any $\mathcal U$-small set $J$. The ordinary coproduct and diagonal functors $\Sigma:\mathcal A^J\rightleftarrows\mathcal A:\Delta$ preserve the coordinatewise weak equivalences, by step 2 for $\Sigma$ and directly for $\Delta$. The comparison of [lem-coef-brown-localization-products] identifies the coherent localization of $\mathcal A^J$ with $L^J$, since each factor has precisely the all-cofibrant Brown hypotheses already checked in step 1. Descend $\Sigma,\Delta$ and their ordinary unit and counit using the entire-functor-category localization property; the descended diagonal is the actual diagonal $L\to L^J$ by restriction. Naturality, triangle identities and their coherence descend too, since restriction is an equivalence on the entire relevant functor categories. Explicitly the unit and counit give inverse maps of mapping spaces: $g:\overline\Sigma X\to y$ goes to $\Delta(g)\eta_X$, and $h:X\to\Delta y$ goes to $\epsilon_y\overline\Sigma(h)$; the two composites are identities by naturality and the triangles, including higher simplices. Thus $\overline\Sigma$ is left adjoint to the diagonal. This says exactly that its unit cocones are coproducts in $L$. On the family $(qX_a)$ that unit is the image of the ordinary coproduct coprojections, so $q$ preserves the asserted coproduct cocones. The product lemma includes $J=\varnothing$, agreeing with step 1. Mapping spaces and coherent equivalences are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 7.1.14 (localization of adjunctions preserving weak equivalences), dual of Proposition 7.7.1 and proof of Proposition 7.7.4; unit/counit descent written explicitly Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Steps 1 and 3 supply all pushouts and all $\mathcal U$-small coproducts in $L$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-small-colimit-generation] to obtain all $\mathcal U$-small coherent colimits. This application imposes no local $\mathcal U$-smallness condition: categories and their mapping spaces may lie in the common larger universe while only the indexing shapes must be $\mathcal U$-small. Together with the actual cocones verified in steps 1 and 3, this proves the existence and localization-functor clauses of the item.

source.place: Dual of Theorem 7.3.22, as used in Proposition 7.7.4; Remark 7.7.10 for the universe scope Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Let $T:N(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal E$ satisfy the stated hypotheses, and let $\overline T:L\to\mathcal E$ be its coherent factorization, with $\overline Tq\simeq T$. It preserves every pushout in $L$ as follows. Apply [lem-coef-brown-finite-direct-rectification] with the span category $(0\leftarrow1\to2)$ to represent any coherent span in $L$ by a strict span $B\xleftarrow{u}A\xrightarrow{v}D$ in $\mathcal A$. Factor $u=pi$ with $i:A\to B'\in C$ and $p:B'\to B\in W$. The natural map of strict spans $(B'\leftarrow A\to D)\to(B\leftarrow A\to D)$ has components $(p,1_A,1_D)$; after $q$ it is a coherent equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The ordinary pushout $P=B'\amalg_A D$ exists, and step 1 identifies its $q$-cocone as a pushout of the replacement span. By the preservation hypothesis on $T$, its $T$-cocone is a pushout in $\mathcal E$. The equivalence $\overline Tq\simeq T$ identifies this with the $\overline T$-image of the $q$-cocone. For an equivalence $e:S\to S_0$ of span diagrams, precomposition sends a cocone $S_0\to\Delta x$ to its composite with $e$; precomposition with a chosen inverse of $e$ is inverse up to the whiskered inverse homotopies. These operations keep the apex and commute with $\overline T$. The cocone categories are therefore equivalent. The dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] shows that initial cocones correspond. Any specified pushout of the original span is equivalent, as a cocone, to the one obtained this way: its mapping spaces to and from that cocone are contractible, so the two comparison arrows compose to identities up to homotopy. Applying $\overline T$ keeps this equivalence, proving preservation of that specified pushout. All objects are cofibrant, so the factorization needs no extra cofibrancy or properness assumption.

source.place: Dual of Theorem 7.6.17 for the span; preservation part of Corollary 7.7.5, with the strict cofibration replacement and cocone calculation expanded Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Every object of $L$ is equivalent to some $qX$, by the singleton case of [lem-coef-brown-finite-direct-rectification]. Given any $\mathcal U$-small family in $L$, choose such representatives for its entries in the common larger universe. Step 3 identifies its coproduct cocone, after these equivalences, with $q$ of the ordinary coproduct cocone of the representatives. Its image under $\overline T$ is identified with $T$ of that cocone, which is a coproduct by the hypothesis on $T$. The chosen component equivalences and their inverses give inverse coherent maps between the two discrete diagrams. Precomposing cocones with these maps, as in step 5, gives inverse equivalences of cocone categories with unchanged apices, and this construction commutes with $\overline T$. The mapping-space cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore proves preservation of the original coproduct cocone. This includes the empty family and hence initial objects. Apply the preservation assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-small-colimit-generation], using step 5 for pushouts, to conclude that $\overline T$ preserves every $\mathcal U$-small coherent colimit.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 7.7.5 and dual of Proposition 7.3.23: check coproducts on representatives, then use pushout/coproduct generation Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: The assumed localization universal property gives an equivalence $q^*:\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_W(N\mathcal A,\mathcal E)$ on entire coherent functor categories. Steps 5 and 6 say that a functor on the right with the stated initial-object, coproduct and cofibration-pushout preservation lies in the image of a colimit-preserving functor. Conversely, if $F:L\to\mathcal E$ preserves all $\mathcal U$-small colimits, then $Fq$ inverts $W$ and preserves those cocones because steps 1 and 3 proved that $q$ does. Thus $q^*$ identifies exactly the indicated objects. Both subcategories in the assertion are full: restricting this equivalence to those objects keeps every transformation and every higher simplex. This proves the transformation clause, rather than merely an objectwise factorization.
